title: Medical Student Acceptance and Perceptions of Augmented Reality Simulation
official: Medical Student Acceptance and Perceptions of Augmented Reality Simulation: A Mixed-Methods, Prospective Study
summary:
This prospective, single-arm, mixed-methods pilot study will evaluate medical students' experiences with, perceptions of, and acceptance of augmented reality (AR) simulation. Medical students completing their core critical care medicine (CCM) clerkship at Stanford University will take part in a single 70-minute augmented reality (AR) simulation session at the Center for Immersive and Simulation-based Learning (CISL).

The session includes one instructor-facilitated pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) scenario using an AR headset. The primary outcome is students' experiences and perceptions, explored through thematic analysis of post-simulation focus groups. Secondary outcomes are technology acceptance (Technology Acceptance Model), usability (System Usability Scale), and ergonomics (ISO 9241-400-based questionnaire).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Between age 18-50
* medical student participate in core critical care medicine (CCM) clerkship

Exclusion Criteria:

* a history of severe motion sickness
* a history of seizures cause by flashing light
* Major surgery within the last 48 hours
